metadata.note: The Hojack Line -- the Lake Ontario shore route from Oswego west through Sodus, Webster, Charlotte (Rochester's lake port) and Kendall to Lewiston, and the last big blank along the lakeshore on this map. The Lake Ontario Shore Railroad was organized at Oswego on March 17 1868 and began construction at Red Creek in August 1871; it was merged into the Rome, Watertown and Ogdensburg Railroad in 1875, and the RW&O completed the line from Lewiston to Oswego on June 12 1876. The RW&O worked it until March 14 1891, when the whole RW&O was leased to the New York Central and Hudson River Railroad (see watertown_rome_railroad.geojson for the rest of that system), and it was formally absorbed into the New York Central in 1913. The nickname is local legend: a farmer whose mule stalled on a crossing at train time was heard shouting 'Ho-Jack! Ho-Jack!' at it, and the trainmen kept the name. Through passenger service from Oswego to Rochester and Suspension Bridge was discontinued on February 2 1935, which is where this map's coverage ends -- the line itself carried freight for another forty-odd years, under the New York Central, Penn Central from 1968 and Conrail, with the last revenue train on March 31 1978, but freight-only years are not drawn here (see ../CLAUDE.md).
sources: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lake_Ontario_Shore_Railroad and https://webstertrails.org/the-hojack-line-story/ (Lake Ontario Shore Railroad organized at Oswego March 17 1868; construction began August 1871 at Red Creek, Wayne County; completed to Kendall 1875, reached Webster 1876; merged into the RW&O in 1875; the 'Hojack' nickname from a farmer shouting 'Ho-Jack' at a stalled mule on a crossing; the Irondequoit Bay outlet bridge was severed in the decades before 1997; Webster depot closed 1964)

https://nyrails.org/railroads/new-york-central-railroad/new-york-central-railroad-hojack-line/ (the 'Hojack Line' was the NYC line between Oswego and Niagara Falls; station list Windsor Beach, Charlotte, Hamlin, Greece, Kendall, West Kendall, Sterling, Hannibal, Red Creek, Wolcott, North Rose, Alton, Wallington, Sodus, Williamson, Ontario, Lakeside, Union Hill, Webster, Forest Lawn, Seabreeze, Lyndonville, Parma, Somerset, West Somerset, Appleton, Newfane, Beebe Road, Wilson, Elberta, Ransomville, Model City, Haywards, Lewiston Heights, River View, Suspension Bridge; RW&O leased to the New York Central and Hudson River Railroad March 14 1891; absorbed into the NYC April 16 1913)

https://www.rochester-railfan.net/hojack.htm and https://www.fltimes.com/lifestyle/local_history/bicentennial-minute-the-wolcott-railroad/ (RW&O completed the line from Lewiston to Oswego June 12 1876; the RW&O operated it 1875-1891, the New York Central 1891-1968, Penn Central 1968-1976, then Conrail; THROUGH PASSENGER SERVICE FROM OSWEGO TO ROCHESTER AND SUSPENSION BRIDGE WAS DISCONTINUED FEBRUARY 2 1935; by 1958 the NYC no longer carried passengers into Wolcott but still delivered freight; last revenue train March 31 1978; by the late 1970s the whole Oswego-Niagara Falls line had been abandoned or sold off in pieces)
geometry_sources: Real-traced from OpenStreetMap (Overpass) over the abandoned Hojack right-of-way -- the line has been out of use since 1978 and survives in OSM mainly as abandoned railway and rail trail (including the named 'Webster Hojack Trail'). Routed leg by leg through Oswego, Hannibal, Red Creek, Wolcott, North Rose, Sodus, Williamson, Ontario, Webster, Charlotte, Hilton, Kendall, Lyndonville, Somerset, Appleton, Wilson, Ransomville and Lewiston; every leg came out within 17% of its straight-line distance and every station matched within 2 km of the trace. 147.2 mi Oswego-Lewiston. Six connector gaps were bridged, five of them under 0.1 km; the one substantial gap is 2.79 km at the Irondequoit Bay outlet east of Rochester -- which is exactly where the Hojack's bridge was severed, so the hole in OSM corresponds to a real missing bridge rather than a mapping error. Parallel corridors (CSX Rochester Subdivision, the West Shore, the Falls Road) were penalised so the route follows the lakeshore line. Simplified with Douglas-Peucker at 20 m.

WESTERN END: this feature stops at Lewiston, because 'Lewiston to Oswego' is what the sources actually date (June 12 1876). NYC-era timetables ran on through Lewiston Heights, River View and Suspension Bridge into Niagara Falls, but that gorge trackage sits in a disconnected OSM component and routing to it produced a 50-mile detour for a 5-mile hop, so it is NOT drawn. The drawn line is therefore SHORTER than the full Oswego-Niagara Falls Hojack.
metadata.not_yet_sourced: No documented route mileage for the Hojack was found, so the 147.9 mi here is measured off the trace and has nothing to check it against -- unlike most layers in this repo. Frequencies and speeds are estimates, not timetables. Also unsourced: the exact opening dates of the intermediate sections (construction started at Red Creek in August 1871 and reached Kendall in 1875 and Webster in 1876, but the line is drawn at full extent from 1876 rather than staged); whether local passenger service on parts of the line outlasted the February 2 1935 end of THROUGH service (the Wolcott note implies trains of some kind called there later, and the Webster depot did not close until 1964, so a local service may well have continued past 1935 -- if so, this layer ends too early); and the charter date, given as 1858 by nyrails.org against the March 17 1868 organization date used here.
metadata.features_note: Two features, same geometry, split at the 1891 RW&O lease.
metadata.line_label_audit: 2026-08-24: line labels normalised repo-wide to "<operating company>: <line name>" -- the company's common display name (legal suffixes dropped), then the line as a passenger would have known it, or its two terminals where the line carried no advertised name. Long intermediate station lists were reduced to endpoints. For features spanning several operators the company shown is the one that ran the line for most of its drawn years. See CLAUDE.md Rule 6.
